**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 (p0037).**

- **What it does:** Section 6.1 binds the Company not to participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and gives HDI the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded consumer site.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** the product category is defined, but the restriction runs "during the term of this Agreement," and Section 4.1 auto-renews the term annually — so the exclusivity is effectively open-ended, not 12 months. There is no automatic performance-based release; the only escape is terminating the whole Agreement, which can trigger a Termination Payment under Section 4.2, and Section 1.6 covers only the initial operational deadline.
- **Approach:** because HDI takes a reciprocal (indeed longer) restriction in Section 6.3 that benefits us, deleting our exclusivity outright would be disproportionate, so I proposed the fallback: cap the Company restriction at twelve months from the Effective Date and release it automatically on HDI's failure to hit the Site operational date or any service level, delivery date or performance obligation. HDI's brand exclusivity and Section 6.3 are untouched.

Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted.
